limitations: 26 epochs rather than published 100; reproduction deviations are not method gains
Rej-F1 and G-mIoU depend on class prevalence
One seed; diagnostics and perturbations do not establish causality
Raw-logit and native-rounded-score AUROC are distinct
key_findings: Clean five-split AUROC macro: Moment Seen71.57/Unseen53.60/gap17.96pp; QD75.62/56.60/19.02pp. QD has higher absolute AUROC and a larger AUROC gap.
A2/A3/C1 unseen negative-score shift worsens ranking; C2 instead has strong unseen positive-score loss offset in part by easier unseen negatives. This is descriptive decomposition.
C2 negative Rej-F1/G-mIoU gaps coexist with U+ false rejection94.66%/97.71%; they are not evidence of better positive retrieval.
7/12 native checkpoints have exactly equal model tensors, scores, IoUs and thresholds to reference. All five differing reference best epochs exceed26.
Pool max-owner shares on U+ average22.6%-29.6%, effective slots7.05-8.15 of10; exact pooling ties nearly absent. No universal single-slot monopoly is observed.
A2 Moment owner/positive-component leader disagreement70.85% on U+ and73.91% on U-; ownership counts are not signed contribution or removal effects.
A2 native-score pair ties34.70% Moment and10.32% QD; raw-logit AUROC51.89/53.05 remains low, so numerical precision does not explain the main failure.
